notes.4: This question caused major problems with candidates showing little understanding. There was also evidence that the manipulation of the formula weight = mass ⋅ g was too difficult for most candidates.
notes.6: Although nearly half the candidates got the correct answer, it is disappointing that over thirty percent forgot to subtract the mass of the measuring cylinder from the total mass in order to find the mass of liquid.
notes.7: Some candidates did not read the question carefully. The backward arrow was clearly longer than the forward arrow meaning that the car must be slowing down.
notes.8: This is the hardest question on the paper. The majority of candidates either thought that F must be equal to the downward force at the 70 cm mark (3.0 N) or they multiplied the 70 cm by 3.0 N and divided by 80 cm.
notes.11: It is point Q that moves towards the surface, thus the pressure decreases as it moves upwards.
notes.12: The question was not done well. Nearly eighty per cent of candidates failed to recognise that if one column falls by 40 mm and the other column rises by 40 mm then the difference in heights would be 80 mm.
notes.15: The question was not done well. The majority of candidates incorrectly deduced that option D showed the position of the bridge at the hottest part of the day.
notes.17: The question was not done well. The majority of candidates failed to recognise that copper, as a good conductor, conducts the energy away from the point of heating, thereby keeping the paper cooler. It also suggests that few candidates have seen the experiment carried out.
notes.27: Candidates should understand that to magnetise the bar it must be in a strong magnetic field and this can be supplied by a current carrying coil surrounding the bar.
notes.32: A large majority showed they did not understand the principles of the variable potentiometer.
notes.36: A few candidates showed an understanding of the workings of an electric motor.
notes.39: Very few candidates understood this question.
notes.key_messages: Candidates found the paper quite challenging.
notes.general_comments: Candidates answered questions 1 , 3 , 14 , and 28 well. However, they found questions 4 , 8 , 12 , 17 , 32 , 35 , 36 and 39 much more difficult.
